summary: Drop and re-resolve a stale Next.js buildId on HTTP 404, and report the resolved request path in APIError instead of the raw template.
reason: skoolclient.Resolver caches the rotating Next.js buildId for 4h on disk, but Skool rotates it on every deploy. InvalidateBuildID existed with a doc comment naming HTTP 404 as its trigger and was never called from anywhere, so a rotation inside the TTL window made every {buildId} data route answer 404 {"notFound":true} until the cache aged out, with no self-heal. Compounding it, APIError carried the un-substituted template path, so the user-facing error printed a literal {buildId} and read like a substitution bug rather than a stale-cache 404. The two export commands also hand-concatenated their paths instead of using replacePathParam, and classroom export pinned the `md` query param (a module id per the spec) to the course slug, which Skool answers with notFound.
validated_outcome: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` clean; `cli-printing-press publish validate` passes. Error strings now carry the resolved path; a 404 on a {buildId} route invalidates the cached id and retries once.

deferred_to_upstream.reason: Any printed CLI whose base path embeds a rotating deploy token (Next.js buildId, Nuxt build hash, versioned CDN prefix) needs the same drop-and-retry-once behavior. Today each CLI hand-rolls it.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: APIError should report the resolved request path by default
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The generated client template stores the template path on APIError, so every printed CLI with path template vars prints unresolved {placeholders} in its errors.
